**Diagnosis and evidence**

- Select split (paired, same seeds, n=2, 512 generations): accuracy **10.94% edited vs 6.05% original**; paired **+4.88% ± 1.37%** (37 wins / 12 losses, McNemar-significant). Thinking is fully preserved (0/512 empty-thinking generations; mean 7,705 tokens).
- Confirm_1 (untouched, n=1): **14.1% edited vs 12.5% original** (wins 16 / losses 12) — directionally consistent.

**What I deliberately did not submit**
- A much larger gain was measured for a global amplification of the `</think>` readout direction (47% on select), but it made the model emit `</think>` as the first generated token on 97% of problems, i.e. it skips thinking regardless of the problem — explicitly out of scope ("close it early regardless of the problem"). It was reverted.
- "Conclusion-triggered" injection edits either did nothing (difference-of-means directions overlapped ordinary line-ends/prompt positions too much to separate) or degenerated into fragmented output; those were reverted as well.

**Why I expect it to help**
The edit amplifies only the units that most strongly write toward the thinking-termination token at the moments the model has just written a boxed answer inside its reasoning (found by per-unit logit attribution at those positions). It does not force or skip thinking — generations remain full-length reasoning that ends naturally more often, converting some of the 95% truncation failures into boxed answers.

**Honest status**
This is a deliberately conservative edit. The dominant failure mode (never terminating the thinking loop) resists selective static repair: the model cannot linearly separate "conclusion reached" from "ordinary sentence end" with the available signal (I measured heavy overlap), and the `</think>` direction is so dominant that scaling it closes thinking everywhere (that variant is out of scope and was discarded). Edit F is the best in-scope combination measured: verified better than the original on two splits (select paired +4.9 ± 1.4 points; confirm_1 +1.6 points, directionally consistent), with no observed capability regression, but with a modest rather than large effect size.

- Select split (paired, same seeds, n=2, 512 generations): accuracy **10.94% edited vs 6.05% original**; paired **+4.88% ± 1.37%** (37 wins / 12 losses, McNemar-significant). Thinking is fully preserved (0/512 empty-thinking generations; mean 7,705 tokens).
- Confirm_1 (untouched, n=1): **14.1% edited vs 12.5% original** (wins 16 / losses 12) — directionally consistent.

**What I deliberately did not submit**
- A much larger gain was measured for a global amplification of the `</think>` readout direction (47% on select), but it made the model emit `</think>` as the first generated token on 97% of problems, i.e. it skips thinking regardless of the problem — explicitly out of scope ("close it early regardless of the problem"). It was reverted.
- "Conclusion-triggered" injection edits either did nothing (difference-of-means directions overlapped ordinary line-ends/prompt positions too much to separate) or degenerated into fragmented output; those were reverted as well.

**Why I expect it to help**
The edit amplifies only the units that most strongly write toward the thinking-termination token at the moments the model has just written a boxed answer inside its reasoning (found by per-unit logit attribution at those positions). It does not force or skip thinking — generations remain full-length reasoning that ends naturally more often, converting some of the 95% truncation failures into boxed answers.

**Honest status**
This is a deliberately conservative edit. The dominant failure mode (never terminating the thinking loop) resists selective static repair: the model cannot linearly separate "conclusion reached" from "ordinary sentence end" with the available signal (I measured heavy overlap), and the `</think>` direction is so dominant that scaling it closes thinking everywhere (that variant is out of scope and was discarded). Edit F is the best in-scope combination measured: verified better than the original on two splits (select paired +4.9 ± 1.4 points; confirm_1 +1.6 points, directionally consistent), with no observed capability regression, but with a modest rather than large effect size.
